item.title: Education Secretary dismisses claims of Grade 12 exam paper leakage
item.description: The National Department of Education has dismissed claims circulating on social media that the 2026 Grade 12 national examination papers have leaked. Secretary for Education Dr Uke Kombra confirmed that the papers shared online are fake.
item.content:encoded:
The National Department of Education has dismissed claims circulating on social media that the 2026 Grade 12 national examination papers have leaked.

Secretary for Education Dr Uke Kombra confirmed that the papers shared online are fake.

Dr Kombra said the Measurement Services Division (MSD), which oversees national examinations, has checked the images circulating online and confirmed that they do not contain genuine examination papers.

"The security of examinations, from question writing to printing and distribution to the provinces is well secured, and any leak during this period is almost impossible. I want to encourage the public and education authorities not to panic but to remain vigilant," Dr Kombra said.

The Secretary urged students and parents not to fall prey to rogue groups or criminals selling fake examination papers for money.

He warned that the Department has systems in place to identify whether cheating has occurred.

“Examinations will be declared null and void if a school is caught cheating. Students will not be certificated, and teachers involved will be terminated," Dr Kombra said.

Dr Kombra stressed that provincial education authorities, Provincial Education Advisers, inspectors, examination supervisors and school administrators must take responsibility for securing examination papers once schools receive them.

He said MSD continues to monitor information, analyse reports and investigate possible breaches to protect the integrity of national examinations.

The Department confirmed that Grade 10 examinations concluded last week without major issues. Grade 12 examinations continue on Monday, October 12, while Grade 8 examinations begin next week.

The Department urges students to remain calm, focus on their examinations and avoid sharing unverified information online, and to rely only on official Department updates.

item.title: Medical screening and registration for police reservist underway in Northern
item.description: The Oro Provincial Government, through its administration, has funded K1 million to train young men and women as Police Reservists in the province. This has been confirmed to NBC News by Provincial Police Commander, Chief Inspector Charles Winuwan.
item.content:encoded:
The Oro Provincial Government, through its administration, has funded K1 million to train young men and women as Police Reservists in the province.

This has been confirmed to NBC News by Provincial Police Commander, Chief Inspector Charles Winuwan.

Winuwan, in an exclusive interview with NBC News, said the Police Reservists Program started some years back, but due to administrative constraints, the program has been delayed until 2026.

PPC Winuwan said the current recruitment of Police Reservists is comprised of those who completed Grade 12 between the year 2020 and 2025 and public servants. The medical screening, mandatory briefing, and registration process for the shortlisted Police Reservists' candidates commenced today and will end on Friday, 16th October 2026.

The medical examination will determine the final selection process of the Police Reservists' program.

On this note, PPC Winuwan said the shortlisted Police Reservists' candidates will undergo 6 weeks of intensive training at University of Natural Resources or UNRE Oro Campus and will be certified to conduct policing duties as reservists in the province.

In the meantime, PPC Winuwan pointed out that those who graduate as certified Police Reservists will be engaged in the upcoming National General Election in 2027.

PPC Winuwan thanked Northern Governor Gary Juffa with his administration to ensure the Police Reservists Program is delivered in the province going forward.

item.title: Koroba township celebrates successful bore-water project
item.description: Koroba Station came alive on Saturday as leaders and community members gathered to celebrate the successful completion of a bore-water drilling program at the Koroba Catholic Mission in Koroba-Lake Kopiago district. Hela Governor Philip Undialu, Koroba-Lake Kopiago MP William Bando, Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu and other delegates joined the community for the occasion.
item.content:encoded:
Koroba Station came alive on Saturday as leaders and community members gathered to celebrate the successful completion of a bore-water drilling program at the Koroba Catholic Mission in Koroba-Lake Kopiago district.

Hela Governor Philip Undialu, Koroba-Lake Kopiago MP William Bando, Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu and other delegates joined the community for the occasion.

Before officiating the ribbon-cutting ceremony to mark the successful drilling, MP Bando thanked the Hela Provincial Government for delivering the project, describing it as a serious and timely investment for the people.

​"The ongoing El Niño drought has severely impacted our communities," MP Bando stated. "This swift intervention to deliver a clean water supply addresses our most urgent and critical need right now. On behalf of the people of Koroba-Lake Kopiago, I thank the Governor and believe further assistance will continue to reach our district."

Governor Undialu said the Koroba project is the third successful bore-water drilling completed so far, following similar projects at Tari Hospital and Komo Secondary School. He said the program will be extended to all parts of the province. He revealed that the drilling project cost the Provincial Government K5 million.

"The Provincial Government has purchased four 10,000-litre water trucks, one for each district. One will be given to the Koroba-Lake Kopiago DDA," he said.

Governor Undialu added that the immediate priority of his government is to respond to the ongoing El Nino drought.

"About K25 million will soon be used to purchase food rations to assist the people. We will put a temporary stop to any other developments if the drought continues and focus on assisting the people," he said.

He said the project is part of the Hela Provincial Government's ongoing initiative to address severe water scarcity following the El Nino drought, which has left many communities, schools and health facilities struggling for clean and reliable water.

The drilling team will now move to other identified sites across Hela Province to ensure more institutions and villages have access to safe and sustainable drinking water.

item.title: Relatives apprehend suspected killer of female teacher
item.description: Relatives of a man who allegedly murdered a female teacher yesterday afternoon (Sunday) in Koroba-Lake Kopiago District, Hela Province, have apprehended the suspect and handed him over to police. Provincial Police Commander, Inspector Mairi Arau, confirmed to NBC News that the suspect is now in police custody. He said police have obtained statements and are awaiting the coroner's report today.
item.content:encoded:
Relatives of a man who allegedly murdered a female teacher yesterday afternoon (Sunday) in Koroba-Lake Kopiago District, Hela Province, have apprehended the suspect and handed him over to police.

Provincial Police Commander, Inspector Mairi Arau, confirmed to NBC News that the suspect is now in police custody. He said police have obtained statements and are awaiting the coroner's report today.

Hela Governor Philip Undialu has strongly condemned the tragic killing of the late Everlyn Warabe at Bura village and called for the full force of the law to be applied against those responsible.

He expressed his sincere condolences to the family of the late teacher and commended the swift action taken by relatives and the Pureni community to apprehend the suspect and hand him over to police.

He thanked the community for remaining calm, respecting the rule of law, and refusing to take matters into their own hands.

Governor Undialu noted that the recent Gun Surrender Program in Pureni and other parts of Hela had removed firearms from the hands of youths and communities, preventing the tragic incident from escalating into another tribal conflict.

"Had we not removed guns from the hands of our youths, this incident could easily have triggered another tribal fight, resulting in more deaths and suffering. I thank the relatives and the Pureni community for choosing the rule of law over revenge," Governor Undialu said.

The deceased's brother, Smith Warabe, said while the family thanks police for the arrest, they do not believe the killing was the act of a mentally ill person and suspect it was pre-planned.

"We strongly suspect there are people behind this killing who influenced him and are now trying to pretend it was just an act of a mentally retarded man.

"We call for a full and detailed interrogation and investigation, not only through interviews at the police station, but officers must go back to the village to find out the truth. Investigate who is behind this, who planned it, and why," he said.

While acknowledging reports that the suspect may be mentally unstable, Governor Undialu stressed that the circumstances of the killing must be thoroughly investigated and dealt with through the proper legal process.

He called on police to conduct a comprehensive investigation and ensure that those responsible face the full force of the law.

Governor Undialu urged the Warabe family, Pureni communities, and the wider Hela population to remain peaceful and allow police and the courts to do their work.

"We must not allow one tragic incident to take us back to tribal fighting. We have worked hard to remove guns and restore peace in Hela. Let us protect that progress and allow justice to prevail. Let other communities in Hela know this is the rightful process to follow," he said.

Late Everlyn Warabe was the first-born daughter of Pastor John Warabe of Bura SDA Church, Tangimapu Council Ward. She was from the Akuma and Kambe Toro clans of Pureni Village, South Koroba LLG.

She was a dedicated teacher who taught for over 10 years at Pureni Primary School and was recently serving at the newly established Ekele Primary School where she was murdered.

item.title: Balob founder honoured for training generations of PNG teachers
item.description: Frederick Stolz, the founding principal of Balob Teachers’ College in Morobe province, has been awarded the King’s Papua New Guinea 50th Anniversary Independence Medal for his contribution to education. Stolz, 91, received the medal from Papua New Guinea’s governor-general, Sir Bob Dadae, at a ceremony at Government Haus in Port Moresby on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
Frederick Stolz, the founding principal of Balob Teachers’ College in Morobe province, has been awarded the King’s Papua New Guinea 50th Anniversary Independence Medal for his contribution to education.

Stolz, 91, received the medal from Papua New Guinea’s governor-general, Sir Bob Dadae, at a ceremony at Government Haus in Port Moresby on Monday.

He established the college through the Lutheran Mission in Papua New Guinea in 1965. Since then, more than 15,000 primary school teachers have graduated from the institution and served communities across the country.

Sir Bob recognised Stolz’s contribution to education, saying his work had helped shape the lives of generations of teachers and students.

Balob Teachers’ College continues to train teachers in Morobe province, carrying on the work started by Stolz and his early staff.

Stolz attended the ceremony with his wife, Lois, and his grandson Brenton Kanowski, Australia’s consul-general to Papua New Guinea, who is based in Lae.

item.content:encoded:
A high-level delegation of donors are now in East Sepik to engage with the administration of East Sepik Provincial Health Authority and frontliners of healthcare to strengthening primary healthcare services.

The team is led by Dr. Rajendra Yadav, head of World Health Organization (WHO) in PNG and 10 delegates from various organizations including UNICEF, DFAT, PATH, and NDoH. Dr. Yadav "We are not here for assessment", Dr. Yadav said.

"We are here to listen and learn from you and the people at the frontlines [of healthcare] and be able to support them", he added.

The delegation was warmly welcomed by the CEO of East Sepik PHA Matthew Kaluvia and Chairman of the Board of Governance Pastor Max Manimbi.

Kaluvia highlighted that investment from donors will be translated into healthcare services needed as Primary Health Care remains a key priority for East Sepik.

Sharing similar sentiments, Pastor Max Manimbi added that ESPHA has a strong team of driving healthcare forward in the province.

"We are big on good governance. If you work with us, we have a really good team to drive this forward" he said.

This high-level delegation visit that will end on Thursday will be led by the administration of East Sepik PHA into selected health facilities in Wewak, Maprik and Yangoru Saussia districts.

item.description: After officially launching the Central province Development Youth Council on Friday, the Provincial Council body hosted its first executive meeting on Sunday at the provincial headquarter in Konedobu. item.content:encoded:
After officially launching the Central province Development Youth Council on Friday, the Provincial Council body hosted its first executive meeting on Sunday at the provincial headquarter in Konedobu.

The meeting was attended by elected members of the council body including chairman elect Tuku Manai ( Goilala), vice chairman Linus Akaina ( Mekeo LLG, Kairuku), secretary Faustina Doboi,(Kuni LLG, Kairuku) and treasurer George Avada ( Cloudy Bay LLG, Abau), and two district community development officers Madlyn Poia ( Goilala) and Luciano Mekeo ( Abau).

The executive meeting sets the pathway in outlining formal implementation plans to be implemented across the province.

The meeting unraveled important agendas in formulating a 61 Days plan for November to December to start implementing vital programs for youths in the entire five districts across the province for the remaining part fiscal year.

The meeting has also unravelled other key priority agendas in having the provincial youth council draw up Five Year Development Plan 2027- 2032 and the Annual Implementation Plan for 2027.

Community Development Advisor, Michael Peter told the executive council members to start rolling out youth data collection in all 288 wards and 16 LLGs across the five districts in the province to structure the 61 Days Plan and the 5YDP for the Central Province Development Youth Council.

He urged the council members to communicate directly with LLG and district youth councils to conduct the Youth data collection for the entire province.

He said the data will formulate the 5YDP, and the Annual Implementation Plan for 2027 ro be submitted to the Provincial Executive Council for budget allocation to implement programs across the entire province.

He commended the madam Governor of the Province Rufina Peter to initiate the formation of the youth council, and LLG, district and the provincial level to implement youth programs for youths in the province.

item.title: Hailstorm affected Pilikambi communities receive relief supplies
item.description: The Enga Provincial Administration, through the Enga Disaster Office, has delivered six truckloads of relief supplies to communities affected by the recent hailstorm in Pilikambi, Lagaip District. The first batch of relief supplies, consisting of bags of rice and cartons of noodles, arrived on Saturday, October 10.
item.content:encoded:
The Enga Provincial Administration, through the Enga Disaster Office, has delivered six truckloads of relief supplies to communities affected by the recent hailstorm in Pilikambi, Lagaip District.

The first batch of relief supplies, consisting of bags of rice and cartons of noodles, arrived on Saturday, October 10.

According to the Enga Disaster Office, the distribution of food supplies is expected to begin early this week, once all relief supplies have arrived in Pilikambi.

For now, the first batch of supplies is being stored at Pilikambi Secondary School.
